questions.text: What happens to scale-free networks when subjected to random node removal?
options: The network disintegrates rapidly
The diameter and characteristic path length decrease significantly
The network remains largely insensitive to the perturbation
The diameter and characteristic path length increase significantly
questions.correct_answer: The network remains largely insensitive to the perturbation

A researcher is studying network motifs in a biological network and generates randomized networks for comparison. Which of the following statements are correct regarding the randomization process?
options: Randomized networks must ideally retain the same number of nodes and edges as the original network.
Randomized networks can have a different degree distribution to ensure statistical significance.
Randomized networks can be generated using the configuration model, to ensure that the degree sequence of the original network is preserved.
Randomized networks can be generated by randomly adding new nodes and edges.
correct_answer: Randomized networks must ideally retain the same number of nodes and edges as the original network.
Randomized networks can be generated using the configuration model, to ensure that the degree sequence of the original network is preserved.

questions.text: The Girvan–Newman algorithm for community detection involves which of the following steps?
options: Remove edges with the highest betweenness first.
Re-compute the betweenness after each edge removal.
Remove edges with the lowest betweenness first.
Remove nodes with the lowest betweenness first.
correct_answer: Remove edges with the highest betweenness first.
Re-compute the betweenness after each edge removal.

questions.text: A researcher is modeling the spread of an infectious disease on a small-world network. Which of the following are true in the context of the likelihood of a disease outbreak?
options: The diameter of the network is an important factor, as it influences how quickly the disease can reach distant nodes.
The clustering coefficient is one of the parameters that determine the likelihood of localized outbreaks.
The degree distribution has no impact on disease spread in small-world networks.
The transmissibility of the disease is independent of the network structure.
correct_answer: The diameter of the network is an important factor, as it influences how quickly the disease can reach distant nodes.
The clustering coefficient is one of the parameters that determine the likelihood of localized outbreaks.

questions.text: Consider the following two statements: a. Statement 1: Reads from the genome sequencing are prone to error. b. Statement 2: Sequence alignment can be used to overcome this problem. Based on your observations, which of the following statements is not true?

Both statements are false

Both statements are false

questions.text: Microbe ‘M’ has 50 reactions that are stuck when grown by itself. When ‘M’ is grown with ‘N’, the stuck reactions reduce to 40. When ‘M’ is paired with ‘O’, the number drops to 42. Which of the following statements hold true?
options: MSI of ‘M’ in the presence of ‘N’ is 0.2.
MSI of ‘M’ in the presence of ‘O’ is 0.16.
MSI of ‘M’ in the presence of ‘N’ and ‘O’ is 0.36.
MSI of ‘N’ in the presence of ‘M’ is 0.2.
correct_answer: MSI of ‘M’ in the presence of ‘N’ is 0.2.
MSI of ‘M’ in the presence of ‘O’ is 0.16.

questions.text: How are network motifs related to the organization of gene regulatory networks?
options: They represent common patterns of gene regulation that appear frequently in the network
They can be interconnected to form modules, which can regulate specific gene sets
They are not relevant at all levels of regulatory networks
They are always independent of the modules in the network
correct_answer: They represent common patterns of gene regulation that appear frequently in the network
They can be interconnected to form modules, which can regulate specific gene sets

questions.text: Which of the following are true about feed-forward loop (FFL) motifs in transcriptional regulatory networks?
options: FFLs are simple sequences of gene interactions with no regulation involved.
FFLs can involve both positive and negative regulation, which helps control gene expression in a dynamic manner.
FFLs are mainly found in eukaryotic organisms and are not present in prokaryotes.
In an FFL, feedback can either increase (amplify) or decrease (attenuate) the gene expression signal.
correct_answer: FFLs can involve both positive and negative regulation, which helps control gene expression in a dynamic manner.
In an FFL, feedback can either increase (amplify) or decrease (attenuate) the gene expression signal.

questions.text: Consider a graph that was constructed by comparing n DNA sequences. If the two sequences can be aligned with a score greater than a threshold value, we assign an edge between the two in the graph. Given this, which of the following is true:
options: Inserting a new node to the graph requires n comparisons
Inserting a new node is a node level task
If all the alignments have the same score, the resultant graph is a complete graph
There will be two connected components in the resultant graph
correct_answer: Inserting a new node to the graph requires n comparisons
Inserting a new node is a node level task
If all the alignments have the same score, the resultant graph is a complete graph
